faqs.q: What are Bolt-On Lifting Tools used for?
faqs.a: Many loads (motors, gearboxes, flanged pipe, machine parts) have bolt holes but no lifting point. A bolt-on lifting tool fixes to those holes and gives a certified lifting point placed over the centre of gravity, so the load hangs level.

faqs.q: What sizes can Bolt-On Lifting Tools be supplied in?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools can be supplied in the size you need (Built to the load interface). Tell us the size or capacity you need, and the application, through the enquiry and we confirm the dimensions and the part number with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do I need to send for Bolt-On Lifting Tools to be sized and quoted?
faqs.a: For Bolt-On Lifting Tools, send us the load weight and where its centre of gravity sits, the load's length and width, the positions of its lifting points, the crane hook height and any headroom limit. And the environment the equipment will work in (indoor, outdoor, offshore, hazardous area). A drawing, a 3D model or a photo of the load is the quickest way to start.

faqs.q: What working load limit do Bolt-On Lifting Tools have?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools are engineered to order, so the working load limit is set by the design for your load and is stated as "to order" in the listing. The rated load is marked on each item and agreed on the general arrangement drawing before anything is made; it is never inferred from a standard size.

faqs.q: Can Bolt-On Lifting Tools be designed for offshore use?
faqs.a: For Bolt-On Lifting Tools, yes. Offshore designs to DNV standards, with witnessed testing and the documentation the project asks for, are available on request.

faqs.q: What are Bolt-On Lifting Tools made from, and what finish does it have?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools are fabricated from Structural steel, grade to the design, with the finish being a paint system to your specification; galvanized for outdoor use on request.

faqs.q: Are Bolt-On Lifting Tools certified, and to which standard?
faqs.a: For Bolt-On Lifting Tools, engineered below-the-hook equipment is built to order. Your enquiry is reviewed by the maker's design engineers, who issue a general arrangement drawing for your approval before anything is made. Each item is designed to EN 13155, load tested before dispatch and supplied with a declaration of conformity, a test certificate and user instructions. Design calculations, material certificates, NDT records and third-party witnessed testing can be added to the order, and offshore designs to DNV standards are available on request. We confirm the lead time with the quotation.

faqs.q: What do Bolt-On Lifting Tools connect to or work with?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools connect the load to the crane hook, so the hook, slings and shackles above them must be rated at least equal to the design load. See our [lifting beams and spreader frames](/c/spreader-beams) for other below-the-hook equipment.

faqs.q: How should Bolt-On Lifting Tools be inspected and looked after?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools need a pre-use check before every lift and periodic thorough examination by a competent person. Rated load, identification and test date are marked on the equipment and the user instructions state how it may be rigged.

faqs.q: How do Bolt-On Lifting Tools differ from Forklift Lifting Attachments?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools differ from [Forklift Lifting Attachments](/p/forklift-lifting-attachments) in its pattern / standard EN 13155; ASME B30.20 / BTH-1 or DNV offshore design on request against Rated with the truck; ISO 3691 capacity check. It also differs in its size range Built to the load interface against Built to the forklift.

faqs.q: Can Bolt-On Lifting Tools be supplied to customers outside the UAE?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply Bolt-On Lifting Tools to buyers in the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond, and ship them with export documents prepared for the destination once they are built. Give us the delivery country, load and drawing details through our contact page and we quote the freight and lead time together with the price.

faqs.q: What is the lead time and how do I get a quotation for Bolt-On Lifting Tools?
faqs.a: Bolt-On Lifting Tools are made to order, so the lead time is confirmed with the quotation: contact us for current lead time. Send the load, dimensions and any documentation you need through [our contact page](/contact) and we reply with a price and a lead time.

faqs.q: What are C-Hooks used for?
faqs.a: A C-hook lifts a coil, roll or sleeve through its bore, with the hook body reaching around the outside. It is balanced so the load hangs level when loaded and the hook hangs level when empty, which is what lets it be slid in and out of the bore quickly.
